answer: For a whisper concert, agents bid to rent a terrace at a harbor. The hash of the auction ID, offer, bidder key and nonce must fall below a fixed target. The broker accepts each proof once, with no free quota for new accounts. Splitting a fixed hash budget across aliases leaves the expected number of valid bids unchanged; extra bids require more computation or rented hardware. New auction IDs invalidate old proofs. This assumes uniform hashes and honest duplicate checks; efficient or wealthy miners can still buy more influence.
